messages.author: e5d0b3c2486cd4e3
messages.subject: labels/breaks out of bounds
parts:
I can't seem to figure out how to fix the following problem. I found the oob argument in continuous_scale, but wasn't sure how to use it. Any way to tell scales to ignore the breaks/labels that are outside the xlimits? sessionInfo at the end, but this is on ggplot2 0.9.1 and scales 0.2.1.

# Works fine
x <- -3:3
y <- -3:3
labels <- -3:3
breaks <- -3:3
gg <- ggplot(data.frame(x, y), aes(x, y))
gg <- gg + geom_point()
gg +  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks, labels = labels)

# Error because breaks and labels are out of bounds
labels <- -4:4
breaks <- -4:4
gg +  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks, labels = labels)

Error in scale_labels.continuous(scale, major) : 
  Breaks and labels are different lengths

messages.author: e5d0b3c2486cd4e3
messages.subject: Re: labels/breaks out of bounds
parts:
Thanks, but I should elaborate more. I don't want to supply the limits. I'm writing a function that allows breaks as an argument and supplies them to scale_x_continuous. However the limits of the data may not be known. But I want to still use the breaks within the limits chosen by ggplot. For now, I have created a function:

breaks <- -4:4
breaksfun <- function(limits) {
  breaks <- breaks[breaks >= min(limits) & breaks <= max(limits)]
  return(breaks)
}
gg + scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaksfun)

Though it would be nice to tell scale_continuous to just ignore breaks outside the limits. The latter was the behavior for ggplot2 0.8.9.

--sundar
